Abez
AY-bez
proper noun
Hebrew Ebets, of uncertain meaning, perhaps “lofty” or “white”; a town of Issachar, named once.

Biblical Definition

Abez was a town of Issachar, listed once with Rabbith and Kishion: “And Rabbith, and Kishion, and Abez” (Josh 19:20). Nothing of its history survives; it is a name in the roll of the tribe’s inheritance and no more. It lay in the portion of Issachar, the labouring tribe of the vale of Jezreel, whom Moses blessed together with Zebulun: “Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents” (Deu 33:18). While Zebulun went out to the sea and to trade, Issachar rejoiced at home in his tents and his tilled fields. Abez, an obscure town of the home-keeping tribe, preaches the quiet blessedness of faithful ordinary life. Not all are called to go out to great ventures; many are called, like Issachar, to rejoice in their tents, to keep the home, till the ground, raise the children, and serve God in the round of common days. The men of Issachar were known as those who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do. Wisdom and blessing are not reserved for the conspicuous; the obscure town of a home-keeping tribe reminds us that God is honoured in the faithful discharge of humble, settled duty as much as in the boldest going-out.

Webster 1828 Definition

A town of Issachar, named once (Josh 19:20); a town of the home-keeping tribe that rejoiced in its tents, preaching the quiet blessedness of faithful ordinary life.

Modern Corruption

An obscure town of Issachar; it recovers the quiet blessedness of faithful ordinary life, God honoured in humble settled duty.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A town named once raises no modern quarrel. It belonged to Issachar, the home-keeping tribe that rejoiced in its tents while Zebulun went out to the sea.

The principle to recover is the blessedness of faithful ordinary life. Not all are called to great ventures; many, like Issachar, are called to rejoice in their tents, to keep the home, till the ground, and serve God in common days. The men of Issachar had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do. Wisdom and blessing are not reserved for the conspicuous; God is honoured in the faithful discharge of humble, settled duty.
